sizeNotes.s25: Two octaves. Small and simple, good for trying out melodies.
sizeNotes.s37: Three octaves. Enough for easy songs with both hands.
sizeNotes.s49: Four octaves. A balanced size for learning and playing songs.
sizeNotes.s61: Five octaves. Most pop, rock and film pieces fit comfortably.
sizeNotes.s76: Over six octaves. Room for demanding repertoire.
sizeNotes.s88: The full range of a grand piano. Nothing is out of reach.

result.alsoPoints: Your answers also point to {keys} keys. {link} (keys outside your shortcuts need the mouse or touch).

level.never: For a first-time player, three octaves is a friendly place to start.
level.beginner: As a beginner, a mid-sized keyboard is plenty to learn on.
level.lateBeginner: At your level, four to five octaves cover the pieces you are working on.
level.intermediate: At your level, five octaves let you play most of what you practice.
level.advanced: Advanced pieces often use a wide range, so you want more room.
level.professional: As a professional, you will want the full range.

genre.classical: Classical music travels across the whole keyboard, so a wider range helps.
genre.fiveOctaves: {genres} music fits comfortably in five octaves.

goal.improvise: Improvising needs room to move around the keyboard.
goal.teach: Teaching means demonstrating across the whole range.
goal.scales: Scales over several octaves need a wider keyboard.
goal.light: For chords, ear training and playing for fun, five octaves is plenty.

cap.never: Since you haven't played before, a smaller keyboard is less overwhelming.
cap.early: You're still early on, so there's no need for the largest keyboard yet.

instrument.acoustic: An acoustic piano has 88 keys, so that layout would feel familiar.
instrument.digital: Your keyboard has {n} keys, so that size would feel familiar.

input.keyboard: About three octaves fit comfortably on computer keys; the rest needs the mouse.
input.tablet: On a tablet, keys stay easy to tap up to about five octaves.
input.phone: On a phone, keys get small quickly, so we kept it compact.

tips.shortcuts: By default only C4 to E5 have computer-key shortcuts. Assign the rest of your keys in Settings.
tips.rotate: Turn your phone sideways to make the keys wider.
tips.noteNames: Every note you press shows its name above the keyboard.
tips.recorder: Use the recorder under the piano to capture a take, play it back or download it.
